## GEOGRAPHY point set intersection
# Source: https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/geography_functions#st_intersection
# The documented point set intersection definition gives these results, including polygon
# boundaries. ST_EQUALS avoids relying on undocumented component or vertex ordering.

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(CAST(NULL AS GEOGRAPHY), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> null

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), CAST(NULL AS GEOGRAPHY))
=> null

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(CAST(NULL AS GEOGRAPHY), CAST(NULL AS GEOGRAPHY))
=> null

SELECT TYPEOF(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0)))
=> "GEOGRAPHY"

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POINT EMPTY'), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY"

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON EMPTY'))
=> "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY"

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POINT EMPTY'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING EMPTY'))
=> "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY"

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 1))
=> "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2)), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('MULTIPOINT(0 0, 1 1, 2 2)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('MULTIPOINT(1 1, 2 2, 3 3)')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('MULTIPOINT(1 1, 2 2)'))
=> "true"

# A line includes its endpoints and interior points. Crossings and shared endpoints become points.
SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)')), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)'), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 0)), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 0))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_ISEMPTY(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 1), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)')))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(-1 0, 1 0)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 -1, 0 1)')), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 1 0)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(1 0, 2 0)')), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 0))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(3 0, 1 0)')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(1 0, 2 0)'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(2 0, 0 0)')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)'))
=> "true"

# Polygon interiors, shell boundaries and hole boundaries are included; hole interiors are not.
SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 4 0, 0 4, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 1)), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 1))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 4 0, 0 4, 0 0))')), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 4 0, 0 4, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(-1 0, 5 0)')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 4 0)'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 -1, 0 5)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 4 0, 0 4, 0 0))')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 0 4)'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_ISEMPTY(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 10 0, 0 10, 0 0), (1 1, 3 1, 1 3, 1 1))'), ST_GEOGPOINT(1.5, 1.5)))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 10 0, 0 10, 0 0), (1 1, 3 1, 1 3, 1 1))'), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 1)), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 1))
=> "true"

# Polygon intersections can have dimension two, one or zero, or be empty.
SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 60 0, 0 90, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((30 0, 90 0, 0 90, 30 0))')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((30 0, 60 0, 0 90, 30 0))'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 10 0, 0 10, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((1 1, 2 1, 1 2, 1 1))')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((1 1, 2 1, 1 2, 1 1))'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 2 0, 0 2, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 0 -2, 2 0, 0 0))')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 2 0, 0 2, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, -2 0, 0 -2, 0 0))')), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_ISEMPTY(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 2 0, 0 2, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((10 0, 12 0, 10 2, 10 0))')))
=> "true"

# The intersection of two mixed collections retains components of every resulting dimension.
SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('GEOMETRYCOLLECTION(POLYGON((0 0, 4 0, 0 4, 0 0)), LINESTRING(10 0, 14 0), POINT(20 0))'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('GEOMETRYCOLLECTION(POLYGON((1 1, 2 1, 1 2, 1 1)), LINESTRING(12 0, 16 0), MULTIPOINT(20 0, 30 0))')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('GEOMETRYCOLLECTION(POLYGON((1 1, 2 1, 1 2, 1 1)), LINESTRING(12 0, 14 0), POINT(20 0))'))
=> "true"

# Full geography is the identity for intersection, including a polygon with holes.
SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe'), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2)), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 1 1)'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 1 1)'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 10 0, 0 10, 0 0), (1 1, 3 1, 1 3, 1 1))')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 10 0, 0 10, 0 0), (1 1, 3 1, 1 3, 1 1))'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_EQUALS(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe')), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe'))
=> "true"

SELECT ST_ISEMPTY(ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('fullglobe'), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POINT EMPTY')))
=> "true"

# SAFE. and conditional expressions preserve ordinary function and short-circuit behavior.
SELECT ST_EQUALS(SAFE.ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2)), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 2))
=> "true"

SELECT IF(FALSE, ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 100), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0)), ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0))
=> "POINT(0 0)"

# Source: BigQuery answers for snapping within a micrometer of a vertex or edge.
SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(0, 0), ST_GEOGPOINT(0.000000000001, 0))
=> "POINT(0 0)"

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGPOINT(1, 0.000000000001), ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 2 0)'))
=> "POINT(1 1e-12)"

SELECT ST_INTERSECTION(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 2 0, 0 2, 0 0))'), ST_GEOGPOINT(1, -0.000000000001))
=> "POINT(1 -1e-12)"
